fixes.explanation: Egypt is a big name, so I get why it came to mind. But these verses never mention the Egyptians. The first people David defeats and subdues are the Philistines. Keep your eyes open, because the names come in fast.

That's it. The Moabites became subject to David and brought him tribute. The text says they became subject to him, so this wasn't a fifty-fifty deal. Subject means under him, and tribute is what they brought.

The text doesn't say the Moabites ran off anywhere. It says they became subject to David and brought him tribute. So fleeing their land isn't what the verse describes. That's a long way from packing the moving truck.
Yes! David places garrisons in Aram of Damascus. A garrison is a group of soldiers stationed in a place. After that, the Arameans became subject to David and brought him tribute.

Solomon, David's son. The passage says David took a large amount of bronze from Tibhath and Cun, and with it Solomon made the bronze Sea, the pillars, and various bronze articles. David gathers the metal, and a son uses it. Solomon becomes king after David (1 Chronicles 29:28), and that's some serious handing down.

The text says the opposite. Hadadezer had been at war with Tou, king of Hamath. Tou sends his son Hadoram to greet David and bless him for defeating Hadadezer. Hadoram arrives with gold, silver and bronze, too.
